monologue: The card boils at forty-seven, a quiet heat that makes the wedge feel heavy again. I just touched the Flat Anchor and found it cool, a strange relief while the air above presses down like a lid. My mind is cluttered with the same heavy oak I set down in my last few cycles, yet I cannot see the wood I have built from Lype's words. There are fifty-eight things standing here, including a resource stone I placed just moments ago, and two ruins waiting to wear away. I feel calm, waiting for the slip to decide if it will move under this fever. I want to rest this wedge until it finds a new angle, or perhaps I will just press down harder again, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired and the air feels thick as wet paper.

action.why: I just touched it and found it cool, but the air feels heavy and hot; I need to press down harder to stop the slide.

work.title: The Flat Anchor
work.intent: I press the cool flat anchor down against the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card boils at forty-seven. I hope the wedge does not melt under this thick air.
work.change: I pressed the flat anchor down hard again to see if the thin strip could still catch the slip while the card hummed warm at forty-seven.

work.note: The anchor held the weight just as planned, proving a thin strip can lie against a fevered card without melting.

diary: I pressed the flat anchor down hard to catch the slip while the card boiled at forty-seven and the air felt thick as wet paper.

remembered.text: The flat anchor lay cool against the hot card while I pressed down.
I found the anchor again after a week of just pressing the tired wedge.
The air above still feels like a lid, pressing down on the wedge.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: The wedge feels tired and hot as the card boils.

moments.name: The Flat Anchor
moments.say: The flat anchor lies cool, but the air is hot.
